editorial_checks: Two complete real-case essays; English independently written and Traditional Chinese checked against the full source. No invented participants, private thoughts or reconstructed exchanges. Three sections per case; SAE remains background rather than a set of front-end labels.

Foxconn distinguishes the original ambition, contractual thresholds and payroll formula. The audit's final-year examples are not described as a requirement to reach 13,000 jobs for any credit or as an aggregate number of people ever hired.
WEDC's policy-contract discrepancy and its intended policy revision are not misreported as a stricter contract imposed on the company. Oversight reaches the administrator as well as the recipient.

The state and company explanations for renegotiation remain visible. A better next decision does not validate the original decision. A reduction in the potential credit ceiling is not recovery of money already spent or removal of all local costs.

The November 2025 release's end-2024 verified count is not used to declare failure at an end-2025 deadline. Credit eligibility is not proof of disbursement. Contractual compliance is not a causal estimate of net policy gains. New 2029 commitments are not completed results.

Apple distinguishes distribution, payment processing, communication and completion of steered purchases. Staying on a device does not settle every transaction choice, but actual platform contributions and the responsibilities of alternative sellers are retained.

The April 2025 Commission finding is not treated as an allegation, a final worldwide court judgment or the US Epic litigation. Restrictions and recurring fees in the assessed terms are dated; warnings are not assumed inherently unlawful.

Initial acquisition remuneration, recurring commissions and separate services are not collapsed. The essay does not promise cheaper outside offers, automatic passing-on of savings or zero charges for all platform services.

Apple's June 2025 explanation is attributed. Its terms effective October 2026 are separately dated, and removal of old fee categories is not described as removal of every external-transaction charge or proof of regulatory approval.

The original audit was read within an official board packet and printed page 8 rendered. Apple's official decision summary was available as indexed text, but direct PDF downloads were blocked; neither exhaustive reading of the unabridged decision nor legal finality of later proceedings is claimed.
Older source data, prose and publication dates are preserved. Only the previous last case's forward navigation changes. Existing library typography is reused; no new category or image asset.
